title: Temporal assertions and jam fault
summary: Latch the jam fault and prove its timing with AT, WITHIN, FOR, UNTIL, RISING, and FALLING assertions.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show a physical fault, physical clearance or target timing.
objectives: Latch the jam fault and prove its timing with temporal assertions.
Require a new Start before the belt moves again after the fault is released.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: Read tests/conveyor-jam-timing.scenario.json next to src/Conveyor.st. Start is pressed at {{t:0}} ms, a jam appears at {{t:30}} ms and clears at {{t:50}} ms, Reset is pressed at {{t:40}} ms (jam present) and at {{t:60}} ms (jam cleared), and Start is pressed again at {{t:80}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: The starter must latch the jam fault (building on lesson 4) before the scenario can pass.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: Before running, predict BeltCommand and FaultLamp at {{t:20}}, {{t:30}}, {{t:50}}, {{t:60}}, and {{t:80}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: Belt ON and FaultLamp OFF at {{t:20}}; Belt OFF and FaultLamp ON at {{t:30}} and still at {{t:50}} (Reset at {{t:40}} is ignored and the jam clearing does not release the fault); both OFF at {{t:60}}; Belt ON again at {{t:80}} only after the new Start.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct this starter omission, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}: The starter misses the jam latch; latch the fault on JamDetected, ignore Reset while the jam is present, release it only with Reset after the jam clears, and require a new Start to run the belt again.
stages.checkpoint: Check reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press Check. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The required scenario is named ConveyorJamTiming and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Compare
stages.body: Match each assertion to the trace: AT at {{t:20}}, {{t:50}}, and {{t:60}} ms pins the exact states; WITHIN at {{t:30}} ms proves the fault appears in the same scan as the jam; FOR from {{t:30}} to {{t:50}} ms holds across the early Reset; FALLING at {{t:60}} ms shows Reset released the lamp; UNTIL keeps the belt OFF until the new Start; RISING at {{t:80}} ms finds the restart.
stages.checkpoint: The recorded trace shows the discrete sequence, not a physical measurement.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: NEVER forbids BeltCommand and FaultLamp ON together in this scenario. A Reset while the jam is present must not release the fault, and releasing it must not restart the belt.
stages.checkpoint: What the assertions check is tested; nothing else is.

hints.text: Build on lesson 4: JamDetected latches Faulted, and a Reset only counts when the jam input is gone; read the scenario times to see which Reset must be ignored.
Clear Requested and StartArmed when the jam appears, release Faulted only with Reset while JamDetected is FALSE, and let Requested come back only from a Start pressed after Start was seen released.

faultCases: The starter misses the jam latch; latch the fault on JamDetected, ignore Reset while the jam is present, release it only with Reset after the jam clears, and require a new Start to run the belt again.
